earlier_scan.source_named: Conrad, Robert J. & Ronald K. Lewis. 1988. Some language and sociolinguistic relationships in the Upper Sepik region of PNG. Pacific Linguistics. (Phonological survey data; not online.)

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid biso1243 (and retired bika1251 Bikaru) reference list.
sources.note: Zero descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) references; only overview/comparative/wordlist/ethnographic items: Conrad & Lewis 1988, Davies & Comrie 1985, Dornstreich 1973, Franklin 1975 & 2024, Laycock 1973, Haberland 1963 wordlist ms., Dye/Townsend/Townsend 1968.

sources.citation: Franklin, Karl J. 2024. Engan fringe languages (North and South). Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 42: 94-110.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; comparative lexicon and relic suffixes of Bisorio, Nete and Sau from SIL wordlists and the Bisorio NT (NTM 1991). Bibliography names unpublished Dye 1967 Bisorio/Iniai wordlists and Edmiston 1986 SIL survey wordlists.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: Conrad, Robert J. & Ron Lewis. 1988. Some language and sociolinguistic relationships in the Upper Sepik region of Papua New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 26 (Pacific Linguistics A-76), 243-273.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Lexicostatistic survey with wordlists (Pikaru 1/2, Bikaru-Bragge, a Bisorio list supplied by Bob Kennel of New Tribes Mission); a full-text search for stress/accent/phonology finds no relevant line. The scan's named source is online at ANU (hdl 1885/253564) but silent on stress.

sources.citation: Davies, John & Bernard Comrie. 1985. A linguistic survey of the Upper Yuat. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 22 (Pacific Linguistics A-63), 275-312.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No statement. Appendix (p. 283 ff.) reproduces Wayne Dye's 1967 SIL wordlists 'in their original form': the Bisorio list carries no stress marks; the Iniai list has sporadic pre-syllable stress marks (i'dihi 'hair', ambulu'tI 'mouth'). Raw transcription only, no rule.

sources.citation: New Tribes Mission / Ethnos360 Bisorio team (Bob Kennel(l), George Walker et al., 1970s-1991). Bisorio phonology / grammar notes and literacy materials (unpublished mission write-ups underlying the 1982 Genesis and 1991 New Testament).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only team ever to have worked on Bisorio in depth; NTM field teams routinely produce a phonemic statement and grammar for translation, which would be the first-hand stress description. Not located online.
